Abstraction

/ab-STRAK-shuhn/ - rhymes with action · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Abstraction means a general idea considered apart from concrete things or specific examples.

On the survey, 'the average commuter' is an abstraction - a rider pieced together from thousands of trips that no single passenger ever took.

Worked Example

'Momentum,' the coach reminded us, 'never scored a point.' You can graph it, argue about it on sports radio, and print it on a whiteboard, but what actually exists is Tuesday's blocked shot and Friday's twelve-point run - momentum is the abstraction we build above those plays.

Abstraction is the exact word because the idea has been considered apart from concrete things: the blocked shot is real and datable, while 'momentum' gathers a hundred such moments into one idea nobody can touch. And note that an abstraction is not sloppy - it can be defined precisely; it just can't be pointed at.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

concept: a defined mental idea, often still tied to examples

notion: a looser, more offhand idea in someone's head

generalization: a broad claim drawn from a stack of real cases

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reality: the world of touchable, datable things

instance: one concrete, nameable case of the idea

Where it sits · how far from real cases it floats — notion → concept → abstraction

notion vs. abstraction: A notion is a loose idea drifting through someone's head; abstraction goes further, lifting an idea away on purpose from every concrete case.

concept vs. abstraction: A concept is a defined idea you could teach, and it often keeps its examples close; an abstraction has been pulled free of examples on purpose - 'justice' with no courtroom in sight.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — abs-

Prefix — abs-: away

Root — tract

Root — tract: to pull, draw

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Abs- (away) + tract (to pull, draw) + -ion (act or result) = something pulled away. Latin abstrahere meant 'to drag away': an abstraction is an idea that has been pulled away from particular things - 'the average commuter' dragged free of any actual passenger - so the word's anatomy is an exact map of its meaning.

Use the root in a new word: traction

Use the root in a new word: traction: In the deep snow the truck's rear tires lost traction and spun uselessly.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / academic

An abstraction is not a flaw: 'velocity' and 'justice' are abstractions and perfectly precise. Reach for the word when you mean an idea lifted away, on purpose, from particular cases. If an idea is unclear because nobody has pinned it down, the word you want is nebulous, this unit's cloud-word - an abstraction can be exact; a nebulous idea never is.
